about: What a clamp comes to, read by two test suites:
A mount is which chord, how far along it, and how far round — two degrees, which
is what a hook clamp has. Resolving one into a placement happens on a station,
where a demo hangs a rig, and in a browser on every frame of a drag, so there are
two of it. This file is what holds them to each other.
The browser is the *writer* for every parent, catalogue piece or imported mesh
alike, because resolving a mount on a drawing's truss means measuring its mesh
and the station never loads one. Which makes the agreement below the only thing
keeping a station's own arithmetic honest.
`chords` are lines along +X in the piece's frame; `at.x` is always zero, because
`along` is measured from the piece's own origin. HUNG_BELOW is 205 mm — a hook
clamp plus the top of a body — which on an F34 puts a hung lantern 350 mm below
the bar, the figure every demo used before there were chords to hang off.
`transforms` resolves a mount into a placement. `nearest` goes the other way: a
point in the piece's frame becomes the clamp closest to it, and how far off that
is — which is what decides whether a dragged light snaps onto the bar at all.

transforms.name: hung under the bottom chord, a metre and a half along
half a turn stands it on top of the chord, looking up
a quarter turn on the top downstage chord puts it on the face
a pipe hangs from its own centre line
a chord this piece has not got wraps rather than refusing

nearest.name: a light already on the bar stays exactly where it is
one dragged below and a little upstage clamps to the near bottom chord
one dragged out level with the bar rolls a quarter turn onto the face
a piece with no chords is nothing to clamp to
